dek.en: Optimum points mump2p at latency sensitive traders, the network holds steady, the community starts a regional battle and five new projects arrive.

en: Optimum spent this week talking to a new audience. After a month of pitching faster blocks to validators, the company started teasing Optimum for Traders and took it to Binance Blockchain Week in Bangkok.

The network itself had a quiet week: the same share of blocks sped up, the same stake behind the gateways. The noise came from the community, with a regional battle on Discord and five new projects in seven days.
Optimum is preparing Optimum for Traders, a product for traders who care about milliseconds. It is hiring a business development lead for it and showed it at Binance Blockchain Week.
Over the week to 28 November, 92.1% of blocks reached Optimum's gateways first, by 232 ms. The stake behind them held at about 3.43 million ETH.
The Optimum Regional Battle pits five regions against each other for 15 TurboCards, and the community shipped five new projects, from a card quiz to a live tournament.

title.en: Optimum for Traders is on the way

body.en: On 20 November Optimum posted that it was working on something for traders who care about latency. By 24 November it had a name, Optimum for Traders, and the company told people at Binance Blockchain Week to ask Kent Lin and David Song about it. Its case, posted on 26 November, is that onchain stocks, options protocols and agent driven trading have brought latency sensitive traders into DeFi, and that whoever sees the price first trades with an advantage. Optimum has not said what the product does or when it ships. A job opening for a business development lead on the trading side asks for someone with strong connections among those traders.

Across 50,278 slots from 21 to 28 November, 92.1% of blocks reached Optimum's gateways before public observers running the standard network, by a median of 232 ms. The spread between the first and the slowest arrival was 184.3 ms on mump2p against 394 ms without it, 2.14 times tighter. All of this compares Optimum's own gateways with public Xatu observers, and both the gateway count and the observer count dropped a little this week. Stake behind the gateways stood at 3.43 million ETH, 0.5% below a week earlier and still about 2.4 times launch day.

title.en: Head votes: 99.68% against a network average of 98.86%

body.en: On 25 November Optimum said that over the previous seven days, node operators running mump2p voted for the correct head of the chain 99.68% of the time, against an Ethereum average of 98.86%. A wrong head vote costs a validator rewards, so the gap matters to operators. The figure is Optimum's own and the post does not say how the comparison group was chosen; operators who adopt new infrastructure early may already run above average.

On 23 November crypto.news reported that mump2p cut the spread of block arrival times by 53%, from 388.8 ms to 181.8 ms, a figure it credits to DefiLlama Research. The piece is careful about what that means: the arrivals become more even across nodes, average delivery time does not halve. Most of its other numbers come from Optimum or from studies tied to Optimum, including an 8.4% rise in builder bids that it calls a model, not a measurement. It also cites the 36 node test on Lido's research forum, which found earlier arrivals on three of six clients and no statistically significant difference.

Flash, now the community manager, announced the Optimum Regional Battle in the Discord this week. Regional communities compete on activity over two rounds, and the five most active regions share 15 TurboCards: five for first place, then four, three, two and one. Members from Vietnam, the Philippines, India and elsewhere have been rallying their regions on X under #optimumregionalbattle.

title.en: Five new projects in a week

body.en: Opti Card by Capzz turns eight questions into a shareable card, and it is this week's featured project. Mmorgs turned six of his Optimum drawings into the characters of Infinity Run. Lie, named Refined on 23 November, built Link Lab, a puzzle about getting a signal through a network. Zunaira published Optimum Network Lab, a nine module course with quizzes and a simulator. And Capzz pointed us to Aethlos, his live head to head tournament, now on its fifth bracket.

Binance Blockchain Week runs on 28 and 29 November at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre in Bangkok. Optimum is not on the official programme, but it asked anyone there to find Kent Lin and David Song, and to ask them about Optimum for Traders.

Opti Card asks eight questions, half about you and half about the community, and answers with a card: your type, your rank, your region and your face. It takes about two minutes and needs no sign in. The cards spread across X within days, which is the best argument for it: people post them. Capzz also runs Aethlos, a live quiz tournament for the community.

note.en: Flash posted this week's upgrades in the Optimum Discord on 23 November: eleven new Refined members. Every one of them now has a page and a card on the register.
